Topics · One God, one message

What can I lean on that will never fade?

Abraham tests star, moon and sun: does it stay? You name what you leaned on that set, and see where it leads.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلَّيْلُ رَءَا كَوْكَبًا ۖ قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّى ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلْـَٔافِلِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So when the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star. He said, "This is my lord."[322] But when it set, he said, "I like not those that set [i.e., disappear]."

Translator's notes

[322] In verses 76-79, beginning from the people's own assertions, Abraham presents a picture of his dissatisfaction as the only logical conclusion one could reach, in order to show them the futility of their false objects of worship.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:76

Translation

But yet for these men there is but small blame, for they too perhaps go astray while they are seeking God and desiring to find him. For they diligently search while living among his works, and they trust their sight that the things that they look at are beautiful. But again even they are not to be excused. For if they had power to know so much, that they should be able to explore the world, how is it that they didn’t find the Sovereign Lord sooner?

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἀλλʼ ὅμως ἐπὶ τούτοις ἐστὶ μέμψις ὀλίγη, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ τάχα πλανῶνται Θεὸν ζητοῦντες, καὶ θέλοντες εὑρεῖν. Ἐν γὰρ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ ἀναστρεφόμενοι διερευνῶσι, καὶ πείθονται τῇ ὄψει, ὅτι καλὰ τὰ βλεπόμενα. Πάλιν δὲ οὐδʼ αὐτοὶ συγγνωστοί. Εἰ γὰρ τοσοῦτον ἴσχυσαν εἰδέναι, ἵνα δύνωνται στοχάσασθαι τὸν αἰῶνα, τὸν τούτων δεσπότην πῶς τάχιον οὐχ εὗρον;

Wisdom · 13:6-9

World English Bible

A man watches night come on and sees a star. He says, this is my Lord. When the star sets, he says, I do not love what sets. Notice what he tested. Not whether the star is beautiful, but whether it stays. His standard is not belief but steadiness. Something that vanishes is not fit to carry the whole weight of a person.

A question for you

Name something you leaned on completely that later set. Which is closest?

If you sayA person
ThenThat is a real ache, and the verse does not ask you to get past it quickly. It asks only: what stayed with you when they were gone?
If you sayA plan or a belief
ThenThat happens to everyone who searches honestly. The Quran respects the person who revises, and counts revising as a beginning.
If you sayMy own strength or health
ThenIt is the nearest thing we lean on, and it sets too. That does not make it worthless. It means it cannot stand alone as a last support.
If you saySeveral of these
ThenThen the pattern is already clear to you, and you have come to the verse ahead of it. The next verses show what Abraham did once he saw the pattern.

Part 2 of 3

﴿فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلْقَمَرَ بَازِغًا قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّى ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمْ يَهْدِنِى رَبِّى لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ٧٧ فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلشَّمْسَ بَازِغَةً قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّى هَـٰذَآ أَكْبَرُ ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتْ قَالَ يَـٰقَوْمِ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌ مِّمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ٧٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people gone astray." And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allāh.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:77-78

Then he moves to the moon, larger and brighter, and says, this is my Lord. When it sets, he gives it the same test. Then the sun, larger than both, and it sets too. Each time what is tried is bigger and better, and each time the test is the same. This answers a common hope: that if a thing is only great enough, it will stay. The verse says greatness is not the measure; staying is.

A question for you

Is there anything you have leaned on so far that has not set?

If you sayNothing; everything passes
ThenThen you and Abraham are standing in the same place. The verse takes one step beyond it, and that step is the one worth examining.
If you sayYes, something has lasted so far
ThenLasting so far is not lasting always. The verse asks what lies behind both: what makes the lasting thing last?
If you sayI am not sure
ThenThat is enough to go on. The next step does not assume you have answered. It shows where the question goes.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِنِّى وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِىَ لِلَّذِى فَطَرَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًا ۖ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, I have turned my face [i.e., self] toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allāh."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:79

Abraham does not stop at “nothing stays.” He turns toward what lies behind the rising and the setting: the one who began the heavens and earth. The Buddha's teaching moves in a similar direction, in its own words: if the conditioned always lets us down, there must be an unconditioned, or there is no way out. The verse names it and turns toward it. You can stop at the observation and still have learned the first thing the verse teaches.

A question for you

Which of these steps is yours?

If you saySeeing that everything sets
ThenA real step, and many stand honestly at it. The verse does not ask you to pass it before you are ready.
If you sayLooking for what does not set
ThenThis is the step many traditions share, and the questions ahead show what the Quran says about what it found.
If you sayTurning toward it
ThenThat is Abraham's step, and it comes after examination, not before it. If you are there, the next questions ask what follows from turning.

Your reflection

What is the first thing you would name when you ask yourself: what do I not see setting?
